The world is a flat 2D 10 × 10 grid with the snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, heading right.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then the snake is 3 cells long, its head is within one cell of the centre, and it is heading right.

nodes.title: Exactly one food item is on the board, on a random empty cell.

criteria: Given food has just been eaten, when the next step starts, then one new food item is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step the agent chooses one of three moves: turn left, go straight, or turn right.

criteria: Given the snake is heading right, when the agent chooses "turn left", then the head moves one cell up.

nodes.title: Eating food lengthens the snake by one cell.

criteria: Given the head moves onto the food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer and the episode's score rises by 1.

nodes.title: Hitting a wall or the snake's own body ends the episode.

criteria: Given the head moves off the grid, when the step ends, then the episode is over.
Given the head moves onto a body cell, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: An episode with 100 steps in a row without eating ends, so a looping snake can't run forever.

criteria: Given the snake has gone 100 steps since it last ate, when the 100th step ends, then the episode is over with its score so far.

nodes.title: The episode score is the number of food items eaten.

criteria: Given a snake that ate 7 items and then hit a wall, when the episode ends, then its score is 7.

nodes.title: The tank is a flat 2D circle of radius 1 (tank units); nothing leaves it.

criteria: Given any fish or the ball, when any step ends, then it is inside the circle.

nodes.title: The ball moves in a straight line at a constant speed of 0.02 per step and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror, losing no speed.

criteria: Given the ball reaches the wall, when the step ends, then its angle of travel is reflected about the wall's normal and its speed is still 0.02.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a continuous heading and a continuous speed from 0 up to 0.015 per step (three quarters of the ball's speed).

criteria: Given a fish chooses heading 90° and speed 0.01, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.01 in that direction (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches is out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the ball's edge (radius 0.1) overlaps a fish's edge (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that fish is out and its survival time is the steps it lasted.

nodes.title: In the first version, one fish sees the whole world: its own position and movement, and the ball's position and movement.

criteria: Given the single-fish version, when the fish observes, then it receives the ball's position and velocity wherever the ball is.

nodes.title: In the second version, 5 fish swim in the tank at once.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when an episode starts, then 5 fish are in the tank.

nodes.title: In the second version, each fish sees only things within 0.5 of itself (a quarter of the tank's width): the ball and other fish beyond that distance are hidden from it.

criteria: Given the ball is 0.6 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball is absent from its observation.
Given the ball is 0.4 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball's position and velocity relative to the fish are in its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every fish is out.

criteria: Given one fish survives to step 1,000, when step 1,000 ends, then the episode is over and that fish's survival time is 1,000.

nodes.title: The episode score is the mean survival time, in steps, of the fish in it.

criteria: Given 5 fish lasting 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000 steps, when the episode ends, then its score is 600.

nodes.title: An episode holds 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 food pellets in a flat 2D circular tank of radius 1.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then there are 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 pellets at random positions, every prey at least 0.3 from the predator.

nodes.title: A prey that touches a pellet eats it, and a new pellet appears at a random spot.

criteria: Given a prey overlaps a pellet, when the step ends, then that prey's pellet count rises by 1 and there are still 8 pellets.

nodes.title: A prey the predator touches is caught and out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the predator overlaps a prey, when the step ends, then that prey is out and the predator's catch count rises by 1.

nodes.title: Prey move like the fish (continuous heading, speed up to 0.015 per step); the predator moves the same way with top speed 0.018 per step.

criteria: Given the predator chooses full speed, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.018 (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: Every prey and the predator sees only things within 0.5 of itself.

criteria: Given a pellet 0.6 from a prey, when that prey observes, then the pellet is absent from its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every prey is caught.

criteria: Given the predator catches the fifth prey at step 700, when that step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The prey score is pellets eaten per prey per episode; the predator score is prey caught per episode.

criteria: Given the 5 prey ate 30 pellets in total and 2 were caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 6 and the predator score is 2.

nodes.title: Each learning method is written from basic array operations and automatic gradients; no ready-made reinforcement-learning algorithm is used in training.

criteria: Given any training run, when its learning method is inspected, then no reinforcement-learning library code performs its updates.

nodes.title: A training run records the agent's evaluation score at 20 or more evenly spaced points during training.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when its record is opened, then it holds at least 20 (training progress, score) points from start to end.

nodes.title: A training run saves the trained agent so it can be reloaded later.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when the saved agent is reloaded in a new session, then it plays the same moves on the same seed as before saving.

nodes.title: The Snake learner learns the value of each move from reward.

criteria: Given a Snake training run, when it finishes, then it has produced a trained agent and a learning curve under SNAKE-01..07's rules.

nodes.title: The fish learner learns a policy that outputs continuous movement directly.

criteria: Given a fish training run, when the trained fish acts, then its heading and speed are continuous values, not picks from a fixed list.

nodes.title: Each world has a random agent that picks uniformly among its allowed actions.

criteria: Given the Snake random agent, when it acts 3,000 times, then each of the three moves is chosen between 900 and 1,100 times.

nodes.title: The scripted snake moves toward the food, avoiding any move that dies on the next step.

criteria: Given food to the snake's left and a wall straight ahead, when it acts, then it turns left.

nodes.title: The scripted fish swims at full speed directly away from the ball, sliding along the wall when blocked.

criteria: Given the ball is due east of the fish, when it acts, then it heads west at 0.015.

nodes.title: The scripted prey swims to the nearest visible pellet, and flees directly away when the predator is in view.

criteria: Given the predator is in view, when the scripted prey acts, then it heads directly away from the predator.

nodes.title: The scripted predator chases the nearest visible prey, and swims in a straight line until it meets the wall when none is in view.

criteria: Given two prey in view at 0.2 and 0.4, when it acts, then it heads toward the one at 0.2.

nodes.title: A baseline agent sees only what the trained agent in the same world sees.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when the scripted fish observes, then a ball beyond 0.5 is hidden from it as in TANK-07.

nodes.title: Each agent is evaluated on 100 episodes, every agent in a world on the same 100 seeds.

criteria: Given a trained agent and both baselines in a world, when evaluated, then each has 100 scores from the same 100 starting seeds.

nodes.title: The learning curve is drawn with the dataviz skill: score against training progress, with the random and scripted agents' mean scores as reference lines.

criteria: Given a finished training run and its baselines' evaluations, when the chart is drawn, then it shows the curve and both reference lines on one axis.

nodes.title: "Beats a baseline" is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the 100 evaluation scores of each; it passes only if the trained agent's mean is higher, significant at 5% after correction for the number of comparisons made in that world.

criteria: Given the trained and random agents' 100 scores each, when tested, then the result states the test, the corrected p-value and pass or fail.

nodes.title: The trained snake beats both the random and the scripted snake under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the Snake evaluations, when tested, then both comparisons pass.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish beats the random fish under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the single-fish evaluations, when tested, then the comparison with the random fish passes; the same for the several-fish version.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish at least matches the scripted fish: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if the trained fish's mean survival is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 95% of the scripted fish's.

criteria: Given the trained fish's mean is 480 steps and the scripted fish's 490, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "trained mean ≤ 0.95 × 490".

nodes.title: In predator and prey, each trained side is compared under EVAL-03 with the random and scripted versions of that side, all playing against the scripted opponent.

criteria: Given a trained predator, when evaluated against the scripted prey, then its catches are tested against the random and scripted predators' catches against the same scripted prey.

nodes.title: The replay plays any saved agent on a chosen seed as a 2D animation of the world.

criteria: Given a saved trained snake and seed 42, when the replay is started, then the episode plays from its first step to its last.

nodes.title: The replay shows the step number and the current score.

criteria: Given a replay at step 150, when it is on screen, then "step 150" and the score so far are visible.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, stepped one frame at a time, and run at speeds from 0.5× to 4×.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is pressed, then exactly one world step advances.

nodes.title: For agents that see only what is nearby, the replay draws each agent's sight circle.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when replayed, then each fish has a 0.5-radius circle drawn around it.

nodes.title: A recorded episode can be watched again later exactly as it happened, without the agent or retraining.

criteria: Given a recorded episode, when reopened in a new session, then every frame matches the original.

nodes.title: Each world has one note of 1,000 words or fewer explaining why its learning method works.

criteria: Given a finished world, when its note is opened, then it explains the method's idea in ≤ 1,000 words.

nodes.title: The note includes the learning curve chart and the evaluation results.

criteria: Given the Snake note, when read, then it shows the EVAL-02 chart and the EVAL-04 results.

nodes.title: The note describes at least one behaviour seen in a replay, including a wrong or surprising one if seen.

criteria: Given the fish note, when read, then it names a behaviour and the seed of the replay where it shows.

nodes.title: The note states the reference check result and explains any gap.

criteria: Given the reference check result, when the note is read, then it states both scores and a reason for any difference.

nodes.title: The reference implementation is trained on the same world, with the same observations, actions, rewards and time limit as the hand-written learner.

criteria: Given the Snake check, when the reference trains, then it plays SNAKE-01..07's rules and stops within QR-01's limit.

nodes.title: The reference is evaluated on the same 100 seeds as EVAL-01.

criteria: Given the reference agent, when evaluated, then its 100 scores use the seeds of the hand-written agent's evaluation.

nodes.title: The hand-written learner lands in the reference's range: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if its mean score is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 80% of the reference's.

criteria: Given hand-written mean 18 and reference mean 20, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "hand-written mean ≤ 0.8 × 20".

nodes.title: In the simultaneous regime, both sides learn at once, each always facing the other's current version.

criteria: Given a simultaneous run, when the predator updates, then the prey it trained against were the prey's latest version at that moment.

nodes.title: In the past-versions regime, a snapshot of each side is saved at least every 10% of the run, and each side trains against opponents drawn from all the other side's snapshots so far.

criteria: Given a past-versions run at 50% progress, when the predator plays a training episode, then its prey come from one of the prey's 5 or more saved snapshots.

nodes.title: Both regimes are compared side by side: every regime's final predator plays every regime's final prey for 100 evaluation episodes.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when compared, then a 2 × 2 table of predator and prey scores is produced.

nodes.title: Both regimes' learning curves are drawn on one chart with the dataviz skill, predator and prey shown separately.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when the chart is drawn, then it shows four curves: each regime's predator and prey.

nodes.title: Each final agent plays the opponent's saved snapshots in order, showing whether later versions do better against it than earlier ones.

criteria: Given the final predator from either regime, when played against each prey snapshot for 100 episodes, then its catch rate per snapshot is reported in order.

nodes.title: Differences between the regimes are tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5%, corrected for the number of comparisons.

criteria: Given the 2 × 2 table's scores, when tested, then each regime difference is reported with its corrected p-value.

nodes.title: Snake and the fish tank are each signed off only when their evaluation passes, a replay of the trained agent is recorded, the learning curve chart exists, the note is complete and the reference check passes.

criteria: Given Snake with every item but the note, when sign-off is checked, then it is refused, naming the note.

nodes.title: Work on a world starts only after the previous world is signed off: Snake, then the fish tank, then predator and prey.

criteria: Given Snake not yet signed off, when fish tank work is proposed, then it waits.

nodes.title: Predator and prey is finished when both regimes have run, COEVO-03..06 are reported and its note explains the result, whether or not EVAL-07's comparisons pass.

criteria: Given the trained predator fails EVAL-07 and the note explains why, when sign-off is checked, then predator and prey is finished.

nodes.title: The several-fish version starts only after the single-fish version passes EVAL-05 and EVAL-06.

criteria: Given the single fish beats random but falls short of the scripted fish, when the several-fish version is proposed, then it waits.

nodes.title: Evaluation seeds are never used in training.

criteria: Given any training run and the 100 evaluation seeds of its world, when the seeds it trained on are listed, then none is an evaluation seed.

nodes.title: Every training run's record holds what's needed to rerun it: its seed, its settings and the time it took.

criteria: Given a saved training record, when it is opened, then the seed, every setting and the wall-clock duration are present.

nodes.title: Each training run (one learner in one world, or one regime in predator and prey) finishes in under about 1 hour: ≤ 60 minutes wall-clock on the laptop, without a graphics card.

criteria: Timed on the laptop by the training record's duration (DATA-02).

nodes.title: A cloud graphics card is used only when a run can't meet QR-01 on the laptop, and costs ≤ $5 per world.

criteria: Checked against the rental bill for that world.

nodes.title: A training run repeated with the same seed and settings on the same machine gives the same learning curve.

criteria: Run twice; every curve point matches.

nodes.title: The replay plays at 30 frames per second or more at 1× speed on the laptop.

criteria: Measured during a 1,000-step fish tank replay.

nodes.title: One side's PPO, step by step
I write each learning method myself and can explain why it works in a short note.
Every agent clearly beats a random agent and holds its own against a simple scripted one, so "it learned" is a fact, not a feeling.
I can watch any trained agent play, so I can see what it learned, including the wrong things.
Each world adds one new idea, in a fixed order: Snake, then fish, then predator and prey, each finished before the next starts.
The world is a flat 2D 10 × 10 grid with the snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, heading right.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then the snake is 3 cells long, its head is within one cell of the centre, and it is heading right.

nodes.title: Exactly one food item is on the board, on a random empty cell.

criteria: Given food has just been eaten, when the next step starts, then one new food item is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step the agent chooses one of three moves: turn left, go straight, or turn right.

criteria: Given the snake is heading right, when the agent chooses "turn left", then the head moves one cell up.

nodes.title: Eating food lengthens the snake by one cell.

criteria: Given the head moves onto the food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer and the episode's score rises by 1.

nodes.title: Hitting a wall or the snake's own body ends the episode.

criteria: Given the head moves off the grid, when the step ends, then the episode is over.
Given the head moves onto a body cell, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: An episode with 100 steps in a row without eating ends, so a looping snake can't run forever.

criteria: Given the snake has gone 100 steps since it last ate, when the 100th step ends, then the episode is over with its score so far.

nodes.title: The episode score is the number of food items eaten.

criteria: Given a snake that ate 7 items and then hit a wall, when the episode ends, then its score is 7.

nodes.title: The tank is a flat 2D circle of radius 1 (tank units); nothing leaves it.

criteria: Given any fish or the ball, when any step ends, then it is inside the circle.

nodes.title: The ball moves in a straight line at a constant speed of 0.02 per step and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror, losing no speed.

criteria: Given the ball reaches the wall, when the step ends, then its angle of travel is reflected about the wall's normal and its speed is still 0.02.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a continuous heading and a continuous speed from 0 up to 0.015 per step (three quarters of the ball's speed).

criteria: Given a fish chooses heading 90° and speed 0.01, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.01 in that direction (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches is out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the ball's edge (radius 0.1) overlaps a fish's edge (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that fish is out and its survival time is the steps it lasted.

nodes.title: In the first version, one fish sees the whole world: its own position and movement, and the ball's position and movement.

criteria: Given the single-fish version, when the fish observes, then it receives the ball's position and velocity wherever the ball is.

nodes.title: In the second version, 5 fish swim in the tank at once.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when an episode starts, then 5 fish are in the tank.

nodes.title: In the second version, each fish sees only things within 0.5 of itself (a quarter of the tank's width): the ball and other fish beyond that distance are hidden from it.

criteria: Given the ball is 0.6 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball is absent from its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every fish is out.

criteria: Given one fish survives to step 1,000, when step 1,000 ends, then the episode is over and that fish's survival time is 1,000.

nodes.title: The episode score is the mean survival time, in steps, of the fish in it.

criteria: Given 5 fish lasting 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000 steps, when the episode ends, then its score is 600.

nodes.title: An episode holds 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 food pellets in a flat 2D circular tank of radius 1.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then there are 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 pellets at random positions, every prey at least 0.3 from the predator.

nodes.title: A prey that touches a pellet eats it, and a new pellet appears at a random spot.

criteria: Given a prey overlaps a pellet, when the step ends, then that prey's pellet count rises by 1 and there are still 8 pellets.

nodes.title: A prey the predator touches is caught and out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the predator overlaps a prey, when the step ends, then that prey is out and the predator's catch count rises by 1.

nodes.title: Prey move like the fish (continuous heading, speed up to 0.015 per step); the predator moves the same way with top speed 0.018 per step.

criteria: Given the predator chooses full speed, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.018 (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: Every prey and the predator sees only things within 0.5 of itself.

criteria: Given a pellet 0.6 from a prey, when that prey observes, then the pellet is absent from its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every prey is caught.

criteria: Given the predator catches the fifth prey at step 700, when that step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The prey score is pellets eaten per prey per episode; the predator score is prey caught per episode.

criteria: Given the 5 prey ate 30 pellets in total and 2 were caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 6 and the predator score is 2.

nodes.title: The episode score is the number of food items eaten.

criteria: Given a snake that ate 7 items and then hit a wall, when the episode ends, then its score is 7.

nodes.title: The tank is a flat 2D circle of radius 1 (tank units); nothing leaves it.

criteria: Given any fish or the ball, when any step ends, then it is inside the circle.

nodes.title: The ball moves in a straight line at a constant speed of 0.02 per step and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror, losing no speed.

criteria: Given the ball reaches the wall, when the step ends, then its angle of travel is reflected about the wall's normal and its speed is still 0.02.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a continuous heading and a continuous speed from 0 up to 0.015 per step (three quarters of the ball's speed).

criteria: Given a fish chooses heading 90° and speed 0.01, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.01 in that direction (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches is out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the ball's edge (radius 0.1) overlaps a fish's edge (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that fish is out and its survival time is the steps it lasted.

nodes.title: In the first version, one fish sees the whole world: its own position and movement, and the ball's position and movement.

criteria: Given the single-fish version, when the fish observes, then it receives the ball's position and velocity wherever the ball is.

nodes.title: In the second version, 5 fish swim in the tank at once.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when an episode starts, then 5 fish are in the tank.

nodes.title: In the second version, each fish sees only things within 0.5 of itself (a quarter of the tank's width): the ball and other fish beyond that distance are hidden from it.

criteria: Given the ball is 0.6 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball is absent from its observation.
Given the ball is 0.4 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball's position and velocity relative to the fish are in its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every fish is out.

criteria: Given one fish survives to step 1,000, when step 1,000 ends, then the episode is over and that fish's survival time is 1,000.

nodes.title: The episode score is the mean survival time, in steps, of the fish in it.

criteria: Given 5 fish lasting 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000 steps, when the episode ends, then its score is 600.

nodes.title: An episode holds 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 food pellets in a flat 2D circular tank of radius 1.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then there are 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 pellets at random positions, every prey at least 0.3 from the predator.

nodes.title: A prey that touches a pellet eats it, and a new pellet appears at a random spot.

criteria: Given a prey overlaps a pellet, when the step ends, then that prey's pellet count rises by 1 and there are still 8 pellets.

nodes.title: A prey the predator touches is caught and out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the predator overlaps a prey, when the step ends, then that prey is out and the predator's catch count rises by 1.

nodes.title: Prey move like the fish (continuous heading, speed up to 0.015 per step); the predator moves the same way with top speed 0.018 per step.

criteria: Given the predator chooses full speed, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.018 (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: Every prey and the predator sees only things within 0.5 of itself.

criteria: Given a pellet 0.6 from a prey, when that prey observes, then the pellet is absent from its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every prey is caught.

criteria: Given the predator catches the fifth prey at step 700, when that step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The prey score is pellets eaten per prey per episode; the predator score is prey caught per episode.

criteria: Given the 5 prey ate 30 pellets in total and 2 were caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 6 and the predator score is 2.

nodes.title: Each learning method is written from basic array operations and automatic gradients; no ready-made reinforcement-learning algorithm is used in training.

criteria: Given any training run, when its learning method is inspected, then no reinforcement-learning library code performs its updates.

nodes.title: A training run records the agent's evaluation score at 20 or more evenly spaced points during training.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when its record is opened, then it holds at least 20 (training progress, score) points from start to end.

nodes.title: A training run saves the trained agent so it can be reloaded later.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when the saved agent is reloaded in a new session, then it plays the same moves on the same seed as before saving.

nodes.title: The Snake learner learns the value of each move from reward.

criteria: Given a Snake training run, when it finishes, then it has produced a trained agent and a learning curve under SNAKE-01..07's rules.

nodes.title: The fish learner learns a policy that outputs continuous movement directly.

criteria: Given a fish training run, when the trained fish acts, then its heading and speed are continuous values, not picks from a fixed list.

nodes.title: Each world has a random agent that picks uniformly among its allowed actions.

criteria: Given the Snake random agent, when it acts 3,000 times, then each of the three moves is chosen between 900 and 1,100 times.

nodes.title: The scripted snake moves toward the food, avoiding any move that dies on the next step.

criteria: Given food to the snake's left and a wall straight ahead, when it acts, then it turns left.

nodes.title: The scripted fish swims at full speed directly away from the ball, sliding along the wall when blocked.

criteria: Given the ball is due east of the fish, when it acts, then it heads west at 0.015.

nodes.title: The scripted prey swims to the nearest visible pellet, and flees directly away when the predator is in view.

criteria: Given the predator is in view, when the scripted prey acts, then it heads directly away from the predator.

nodes.title: The scripted predator chases the nearest visible prey, and swims in a straight line until it meets the wall when none is in view.

criteria: Given two prey in view at 0.2 and 0.4, when it acts, then it heads toward the one at 0.2.

nodes.title: A baseline agent sees only what the trained agent in the same world sees.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when the scripted fish observes, then a ball beyond 0.5 is hidden from it as in TANK-07.

nodes.title: Each agent is evaluated on 100 episodes, every agent in a world on the same 100 seeds.

criteria: Given a trained agent and both baselines in a world, when evaluated, then each has 100 scores from the same 100 starting seeds.

nodes.title: The learning curve is drawn with the dataviz skill: score against training progress, with the random and scripted agents' mean scores as reference lines.

criteria: Given a finished training run and its baselines' evaluations, when the chart is drawn, then it shows the curve and both reference lines on one axis.

nodes.title: "Beats a baseline" is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the 100 evaluation scores of each; it passes only if the trained agent's mean is higher, significant at 5% after correction for the number of comparisons made in that world.

criteria: Given the trained and random agents' 100 scores each, when tested, then the result states the test, the corrected p-value and pass or fail.

nodes.title: The trained snake beats both the random and the scripted snake under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the Snake evaluations, when tested, then both comparisons pass.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish beats the random fish under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the single-fish evaluations, when tested, then the comparison with the random fish passes; the same for the several-fish version.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish at least matches the scripted fish: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if the trained fish's mean survival is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 95% of the scripted fish's.

criteria: Given the trained fish's mean is 480 steps and the scripted fish's 490, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "trained mean ≤ 0.95 × 490".

nodes.title: In predator and prey, each trained side is compared under EVAL-03 with the random and scripted versions of that side, all playing against the scripted opponent.

criteria: Given a trained predator, when evaluated against the scripted prey, then its catches are tested against the random and scripted predators' catches against the same scripted prey.

nodes.title: The replay plays any saved agent on a chosen seed as a 2D animation of the world.

criteria: Given a saved trained snake and seed 42, when the replay is started, then the episode plays from its first step to its last.

nodes.title: The replay shows the step number and the current score.

criteria: Given a replay at step 150, when it is on screen, then "step 150" and the score so far are visible.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, stepped one frame at a time, and run at speeds from 0.5× to 4×.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is pressed, then exactly one world step advances.

nodes.title: For agents that see only what is nearby, the replay draws each agent's sight circle.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when replayed, then each fish has a 0.5-radius circle drawn around it.

nodes.title: A recorded episode can be watched again later exactly as it happened, without the agent or retraining.

criteria: Given a recorded episode, when reopened in a new session, then every frame matches the original.

nodes.title: Each world has one note of 1,000 words or fewer explaining why its learning method works.

criteria: Given a finished world, when its note is opened, then it explains the method's idea in ≤ 1,000 words.

nodes.title: The note includes the learning curve chart and the evaluation results.

criteria: Given the Snake note, when read, then it shows the EVAL-02 chart and the EVAL-04 results.

nodes.title: The note describes at least one behaviour seen in a replay, including a wrong or surprising one if seen.

criteria: Given the fish note, when read, then it names a behaviour and the seed of the replay where it shows.

nodes.title: The note states the reference check result and explains any gap.

criteria: Given the reference check result, when the note is read, then it states both scores and a reason for any difference.

nodes.title: The reference implementation is trained on the same world, with the same observations, actions, rewards and time limit as the hand-written learner.

criteria: Given the Snake check, when the reference trains, then it plays SNAKE-01..07's rules and stops within QR-01's limit.

nodes.title: The reference is evaluated on the same 100 seeds as EVAL-01.

criteria: Given the reference agent, when evaluated, then its 100 scores use the seeds of the hand-written agent's evaluation.

nodes.title: The hand-written learner lands in the reference's range: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if its mean score is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 80% of the reference's.

criteria: Given hand-written mean 18 and reference mean 20, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "hand-written mean ≤ 0.8 × 20".

nodes.title: In the simultaneous regime, both sides learn at once, each always facing the other's current version.

criteria: Given a simultaneous run, when the predator updates, then the prey it trained against were the prey's latest version at that moment.

nodes.title: In the past-versions regime, a snapshot of each side is saved at least every 10% of the run, and each side trains against opponents drawn from all the other side's snapshots so far.

criteria: Given a past-versions run at 50% progress, when the predator plays a training episode, then its prey come from one of the prey's 5 or more saved snapshots.

nodes.title: Both regimes are compared side by side: every regime's final predator plays every regime's final prey for 100 evaluation episodes.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when compared, then a 2 × 2 table of predator and prey scores is produced.

nodes.title: Both regimes' learning curves are drawn on one chart with the dataviz skill, predator and prey shown separately.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when the chart is drawn, then it shows four curves: each regime's predator and prey.

nodes.title: Each final agent plays the opponent's saved snapshots in order, showing whether later versions do better against it than earlier ones.

criteria: Given the final predator from either regime, when played against each prey snapshot for 100 episodes, then its catch rate per snapshot is reported in order.

nodes.title: Differences between the regimes are tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5%, corrected for the number of comparisons.

criteria: Given the 2 × 2 table's scores, when tested, then each regime difference is reported with its corrected p-value.

nodes.title: Snake and the fish tank are each signed off only when their evaluation passes, a replay of the trained agent is recorded, the learning curve chart exists, the note is complete and the reference check passes.

criteria: Given Snake with every item but the note, when sign-off is checked, then it is refused, naming the note.

nodes.title: Work on a world starts only after the previous world is signed off: Snake, then the fish tank, then predator and prey.

criteria: Given Snake not yet signed off, when fish tank work is proposed, then it waits.

nodes.title: Predator and prey is finished when both regimes have run, COEVO-03..06 are reported and its note explains the result, whether or not EVAL-07's comparisons pass.

criteria: Given the trained predator fails EVAL-07 and the note explains why, when sign-off is checked, then predator and prey is finished.

nodes.title: The several-fish version starts only after the single-fish version passes EVAL-05 and EVAL-06.

criteria: Given the single fish beats random but falls short of the scripted fish, when the several-fish version is proposed, then it waits.

nodes.title: Evaluation seeds are never used in training.

criteria: Given any training run and the 100 evaluation seeds of its world, when the seeds it trained on are listed, then none is an evaluation seed.

nodes.title: Every training run's record holds what's needed to rerun it: its seed, its settings and the time it took.

criteria: Given a saved training record, when it is opened, then the seed, every setting and the wall-clock duration are present.

nodes.title: Each training run (one learner in one world, or one regime in predator and prey) finishes in under about 1 hour: ≤ 60 minutes wall-clock on the laptop, without a graphics card.

criteria: Timed on the laptop by the training record's duration (DATA-02).

nodes.title: A cloud graphics card is used only when a run can't meet QR-01 on the laptop, and costs ≤ $5 per world.

criteria: Checked against the rental bill for that world.

nodes.title: A training run repeated with the same seed and settings on the same machine gives the same learning curve.

criteria: Run twice; every curve point matches.

nodes.title: The replay plays at 30 frames per second or more at 1× speed on the laptop.

criteria: Measured during a 1,000-step fish tank replay.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then the snake is 3 cells long, its head is within one cell of the centre, and it is heading right.

nodes.title: Exactly one food item is on the board, on a random empty cell.

criteria: Given food has just been eaten, when the next step starts, then one new food item is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step the agent chooses one of three moves: turn left, go straight, or turn right.

criteria: Given the snake is heading right, when the agent chooses "turn left", then the head moves one cell up.

nodes.title: Eating food lengthens the snake by one cell.

criteria: Given the head moves onto the food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer and the episode's score rises by 1.

nodes.title: Hitting a wall or the snake's own body ends the episode.

criteria: Given the head moves off the grid, when the step ends, then the episode is over.
Given the head moves onto a body cell, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: An episode with 100 steps in a row without eating ends, so a looping snake can't run forever.

criteria: Given the snake has gone 100 steps since it last ate, when the 100th step ends, then the episode is over with its score so far.

nodes.title: The episode score is the number of food items eaten.

criteria: Given a snake that ate 7 items and then hit a wall, when the episode ends, then its score is 7.

nodes.title: The tank is a flat 2D circle of radius 1 (tank units); nothing leaves it.

criteria: Given any fish or the ball, when any step ends, then it is inside the circle.

nodes.title: The ball moves in a straight line at a constant speed of 0.02 per step and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror, losing no speed.

criteria: Given the ball reaches the wall, when the step ends, then its angle of travel is reflected about the wall's normal and its speed is still 0.02.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a continuous heading and a continuous speed from 0 up to 0.015 per step (three quarters of the ball's speed).

criteria: Given a fish chooses heading 90° and speed 0.01, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.01 in that direction (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches is out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the ball's centre (radius 0.1) is at most 0.13 from a fish's centre (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that fish is out and its survival time is the steps it lasted.
Given the ball's centre is 0.1301 from a fish's centre, when the step ends, then that fish is still in.

nodes.title: In the first version, one fish sees the whole world: its own position and movement, and the ball's position and movement.

criteria: Given the single-fish version, when the fish observes, then it receives the ball's position and velocity wherever the ball is.

nodes.title: In the second version, 5 fish swim in the tank at once.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when an episode starts, then 5 fish are in the tank.

nodes.title: In the second version, each fish sees only things within 0.5 of itself (a quarter of the tank's width): the ball and other fish beyond that distance are hidden from it.

criteria: Given the ball is 0.6 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball is absent from its observation.
Given the ball is 0.4 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball's position and velocity relative to the fish are in its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every fish is out.

criteria: Given one fish survives to step 1,000, when step 1,000 ends, then the episode is over and that fish's survival time is 1,000.

nodes.title: The episode score is the mean survival time, in steps, of the fish in it.

criteria: Given 5 fish lasting 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000 steps, when the episode ends, then its score is 600.

nodes.title: An episode holds 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 food pellets in a flat 2D circular tank of radius 1.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then there are 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 pellets at random positions, every prey at least 0.3 from the predator.

nodes.title: A prey that touches a pellet eats it, and a new pellet appears at a random spot.

criteria: Given a prey's centre (radius 0.03) is at most 0.05 from a pellet's centre (radius 0.02), when the step ends, then that prey's pellet count rises by 1 and there are still 8 pellets.

nodes.title: A prey the predator touches is caught and out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the predator's centre (radius 0.04) is at most 0.07 from a prey's centre (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that prey is out and the predator's catch count rises by 1.

nodes.title: Prey move like the fish (continuous heading, speed up to 0.015 per step); the predator moves the same way with top speed 0.018 per step.

criteria: Given the predator chooses full speed, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.018 (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: Every prey and the predator sees only things within 0.5 of itself.

criteria: Given a pellet 0.6 from a prey, when that prey observes, then the pellet is absent from its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every prey is caught.

criteria: Given the predator catches the fifth prey at step 700, when that step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The prey score is pellets eaten per prey per episode; the predator score is prey caught per episode.

criteria: Given the 5 prey ate 30 pellets in total and 2 were caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 6 and the predator score is 2.

nodes.title: Each learning method is written from basic array operations and automatic gradients; no ready-made reinforcement-learning algorithm is used in training.

criteria: Given any training run, when its learning method is inspected, then no reinforcement-learning library code performs its updates.

nodes.title: A training run records the agent's evaluation score at 20 or more evenly spaced points during training.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when its record is opened, then it holds at least 20 (training progress, score) points from start to end.

nodes.title: A training run saves the trained agent so it can be reloaded later.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when the saved agent is reloaded in a new session, then it plays the same moves on the same seed as before saving.

nodes.title: The Snake learner learns the value of each move from reward.

criteria: Given a Snake training run, when it finishes, then it has produced a trained agent and a learning curve under SNAKE-01..07's rules.

nodes.title: The fish learner learns a policy that outputs continuous movement directly.

criteria: Given a fish training run, when the trained fish acts, then its heading and speed are continuous values, not picks from a fixed list.

nodes.title: Each world has a random agent that picks uniformly among its allowed actions.

criteria: Given the Snake random agent, when it acts 3,000 times, then each of the three moves is chosen between 900 and 1,100 times.

nodes.title: The scripted snake moves toward the food, avoiding any move that dies on the next step.

criteria: Given food to the snake's left and a wall straight ahead, when it acts, then it turns left.

nodes.title: The scripted fish swims at full speed directly away from the ball, sliding along the wall when blocked.

criteria: Given the ball is due east of the fish, when it acts, then it heads west at 0.015.

nodes.title: The scripted prey swims to the nearest visible pellet, and flees directly away when the predator is in view.

criteria: Given the predator is in view, when the scripted prey acts, then it heads directly away from the predator.

nodes.title: The scripted predator chases the nearest visible prey, and swims in a straight line until it meets the wall when none is in view.

criteria: Given two prey in view at 0.2 and 0.4, when it acts, then it heads toward the one at 0.2.

nodes.title: A baseline agent sees only what the trained agent in the same world sees.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when the scripted fish observes, then a ball beyond 0.5 is hidden from it as in TANK-07.

nodes.title: Each agent is evaluated on 100 episodes, every agent in a world on the same 100 seeds.

criteria: Given a trained agent and both baselines in a world, when evaluated, then each has 100 scores from the same 100 starting seeds.

nodes.title: The learning curve is drawn with the dataviz skill: score against training progress, with the random and scripted agents' mean scores as reference lines.

criteria: Given a finished training run and its baselines' evaluations, when the chart is drawn, then it shows the curve and both reference lines on one axis.

nodes.title: "Beats a baseline" is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the 100 evaluation scores of each; it passes only if the trained agent's mean is higher, significant at 5% after correction for the number of comparisons made in that world.

criteria: Given the trained and random agents' 100 scores each, when tested, then the result states the test, the corrected p-value and pass or fail.

nodes.title: The trained snake beats both the random and the scripted snake under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the Snake evaluations, when tested, then both comparisons pass.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish beats the random fish under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the single-fish evaluations, when tested, then the comparison with the random fish passes; the same for the several-fish version.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish at least matches the scripted fish: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if the trained fish's mean survival is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 95% of the scripted fish's.

criteria: Given the trained fish's mean is 480 steps and the scripted fish's 490, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "trained mean ≤ 0.95 × 490".

nodes.title: In predator and prey, each trained side is compared under EVAL-03 with the random and scripted versions of that side, all playing against the scripted opponent.

criteria: Given a trained predator, when evaluated against the scripted prey, then its catches are tested against the random and scripted predators' catches against the same scripted prey.

nodes.title: The replay plays any saved agent on a chosen seed as a 2D animation of the world.

nodes.title: The replay shows the step number and the current score.

criteria: Given a replay at step 150, when it is on screen, then "step 150" and the score so far are visible.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, stepped one frame at a time, and run at speeds from 0.5× to 4×.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is pressed, then exactly one world step advances.

nodes.title: For agents that see only what is nearby, the replay draws each agent's sight circle.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when replayed, then each fish has a 0.5-radius circle drawn around it.

nodes.title: A recorded episode can be watched again later exactly as it happened, without the agent or retraining.

criteria: Given a recorded episode, when reopened in a new session, then every frame matches the original.

nodes.title: Each world has one note of 1,000 words or fewer explaining why its learning method works.

criteria: Given a finished world, when its note is opened, then it explains the method's idea in ≤ 1,000 words.

nodes.title: The note includes the learning curve chart and the evaluation results.

criteria: Given the Snake note, when read, then it shows the EVAL-02 chart and the EVAL-04 results.

nodes.title: The note describes at least one behaviour seen in a replay, including a wrong or surprising one if seen.

criteria: Given the fish note, when read, then it names a behaviour and the seed of the replay where it shows.

nodes.title: The note states the reference check result and explains any gap.

criteria: Given the reference check result, when the note is read, then it states both scores and a reason for any difference.

nodes.title: The reference implementation is trained on the same world, with the same observations, actions, rewards and time limit as the hand-written learner.

criteria: Given the Snake check, when the reference trains, then it plays SNAKE-01..07's rules and stops within QR-01's limit.

nodes.title: The reference is evaluated on the same 100 seeds as EVAL-01.

criteria: Given the reference agent, when evaluated, then its 100 scores use the seeds of the hand-written agent's evaluation.

nodes.title: The hand-written learner lands in the reference's range: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if its mean score is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 80% of the reference's.

criteria: Given hand-written mean 18 and reference mean 20, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "hand-written mean ≤ 0.8 × 20".

nodes.title: In the simultaneous regime, both sides learn at once, each always facing the other's current version.

criteria: Given a simultaneous run, when the predator updates, then the prey it trained against were the prey's latest version at that moment.

nodes.title: In the past-versions regime, a snapshot of each side is saved at least every 10% of the run, and each side trains against opponents drawn from all the other side's snapshots so far.

nodes.title: Both regimes are compared side by side: every regime's final predator plays every regime's final prey for 100 evaluation episodes.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when compared, then a 2 × 2 table of predator and prey scores is produced.

nodes.title: Both regimes' learning curves are drawn on one chart with the dataviz skill, predator and prey shown separately.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when the chart is drawn, then it shows four curves: each regime's predator and prey.

nodes.title: Each final agent plays the opponent's saved snapshots in order, showing whether later versions do better against it than earlier ones.

criteria: Given the final predator from either regime, when played against each prey snapshot for 100 episodes, then its catch rate per snapshot is reported in order.

nodes.title: Differences between the regimes are tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5%, corrected for the number of comparisons.

criteria: Given the 2 × 2 table's scores, when tested, then each regime difference is reported with its corrected p-value.

nodes.title: I write each learning method myself and can explain why it works in a short note.
Every agent clearly beats a random agent and holds its own against a simple scripted one, so "it learned" is a fact, not a feeling.
I can watch any trained agent play, so I can see what it learned, including the wrong things.
Each world adds one new idea, in a fixed order: Snake, then fish, then predator and prey, each finished before the next starts.
The world is a flat 2D 10 × 10 grid with the snake starting 3 cells long in the middle, heading right.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then the snake is 3 cells long, its head is within one cell of the centre, and it is heading right.

nodes.title: Exactly one food item is on the board, on a random empty cell.

criteria: Given food has just been eaten, when the next step starts, then one new food item is on a cell the snake does not occupy.

nodes.title: Each step the agent chooses one of three moves: turn left, go straight, or turn right.

criteria: Given the snake is heading right, when the agent chooses "turn left", then the head moves one cell up.

nodes.title: Eating food lengthens the snake by one cell.

criteria: Given the head moves onto the food, when the step ends, then the snake is one cell longer and the episode's score rises by 1.

nodes.title: Hitting a wall or the snake's own body ends the episode.

criteria: Given the head moves off the grid, when the step ends, then the episode is over.
Given the head moves onto a body cell, when the step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: An episode with 100 steps in a row without eating ends, so a looping snake can't run forever.

criteria: Given the snake has gone 100 steps since it last ate, when the 100th step ends, then the episode is over with its score so far.

nodes.title: The episode score is the number of food items eaten.

criteria: Given a snake that ate 7 items and then hit a wall, when the episode ends, then its score is 7.

nodes.title: The tank is a flat 2D circle of radius 1 (tank units); nothing leaves it.

criteria: Given any fish or the ball, when any step ends, then it is inside the circle.

nodes.title: The ball moves in a straight line at a constant speed of 0.02 per step and bounces off the tank wall like a mirror, losing no speed.

criteria: Given the ball reaches the wall, when the step ends, then its angle of travel is reflected about the wall's normal and its speed is still 0.02.

nodes.title: Each step a fish chooses a continuous heading and a continuous speed from 0 up to 0.015 per step (three quarters of the ball's speed).

criteria: Given a fish chooses heading 90° and speed 0.01, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.01 in that direction (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: A fish the ball touches is out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the ball's centre (radius 0.1) is at most 0.13 from a fish's centre (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that fish is out and its survival time is the steps it lasted.
Given the ball's centre is 0.1301 from a fish's centre, when the step ends, then that fish is still in.

nodes.title: In the first version, one fish sees the whole world: its own position and movement, and the ball's position and movement.

criteria: Given the single-fish version, when the fish observes, then it receives the ball's position and velocity wherever the ball is.

nodes.title: In the second version, 5 fish swim in the tank at once.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when an episode starts, then 5 fish are in the tank.

nodes.title: In the second version, each fish sees only things within 0.5 of itself (a quarter of the tank's width): the ball and other fish beyond that distance are hidden from it.

criteria: Given the ball is 0.6 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball is absent from its observation.
Given the ball is 0.4 from a fish, when that fish observes, then the ball's position and velocity relative to the fish are in its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every fish is out.

criteria: Given one fish survives to step 1,000, when step 1,000 ends, then the episode is over and that fish's survival time is 1,000.

nodes.title: The episode score is the mean survival time, in steps, of the fish in it.

criteria: Given 5 fish lasting 200, 400, 600, 800 and 1,000 steps, when the episode ends, then its score is 600.

nodes.title: An episode holds 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 food pellets in a flat 2D circular tank of radius 1.

criteria: Given a new episode, when it starts, then there are 5 prey, 1 predator and 8 pellets at random positions, every prey at least 0.3 from the predator.

nodes.title: A prey that touches a pellet eats it, and a new pellet appears at a random spot.

criteria: Given a prey's centre (radius 0.03) is at most 0.05 from a pellet's centre (radius 0.02), when the step ends, then that prey's pellet count rises by 1 and there are still 8 pellets.

nodes.title: A prey the predator touches is caught and out for the rest of the episode.

criteria: Given the predator's centre (radius 0.04) is at most 0.07 from a prey's centre (radius 0.03), when the step ends, then that prey is out and the predator's catch count rises by 1.

nodes.title: Prey move like the fish (continuous heading, speed up to 0.015 per step); the predator moves the same way with top speed 0.018 per step.

criteria: Given the predator chooses full speed, when the step ends, then it has moved 0.018 (unless stopped by the wall).

nodes.title: Every prey and the predator sees only things within 0.5 of itself.

criteria: Given a pellet 0.6 from a prey, when that prey observes, then the pellet is absent from its observation.

nodes.title: An episode ends after 1,000 steps or when every prey is caught.

criteria: Given the predator catches the fifth prey at step 700, when that step ends, then the episode is over.

nodes.title: The prey score is pellets eaten per prey per episode; the predator score is prey caught per episode.

criteria: Given the 5 prey ate 30 pellets in total and 2 were caught, when the episode ends, then the prey score is 6 and the predator score is 2.

nodes.title: Each learning method is written from basic array operations and automatic gradients; no ready-made reinforcement-learning algorithm is used in training.

criteria: Given any training run, when its learning method is inspected, then no reinforcement-learning library code performs its updates.

nodes.title: A training run records the agent's evaluation score at 20 or more evenly spaced points during training.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when its record is opened, then it holds at least 20 (training progress, score) points from start to end.

nodes.title: A training run saves the trained agent so it can be reloaded later.

criteria: Given a finished training run, when the saved agent is reloaded in a new session, then it plays the same moves on the same seed as before saving.

nodes.title: The Snake learner learns the value of each move from reward.

criteria: Given a Snake training run, when it finishes, then it has produced a trained agent and a learning curve under SNAKE-01..07's rules.

nodes.title: The fish learner learns a policy that outputs continuous movement directly.

criteria: Given a fish training run, when the trained fish acts, then its heading and speed are continuous values, not picks from a fixed list.

nodes.title: Each world has a random agent that picks uniformly among its allowed actions.

criteria: Given the Snake random agent, when it acts 3,000 times, then each of the three moves is chosen between 900 and 1,100 times.

nodes.title: The scripted snake moves toward the food, avoiding any move that dies on the next step.

criteria: Given food to the snake's left and a wall straight ahead, when it acts, then it turns left.

nodes.title: The scripted fish swims at full speed directly away from the ball, sliding along the wall when blocked.

criteria: Given the ball is due east of the fish, when it acts, then it heads west at 0.015.

nodes.title: The scripted prey swims to the nearest visible pellet, and flees directly away when the predator is in view.

criteria: Given the predator is in view, when the scripted prey acts, then it heads directly away from the predator.

nodes.title: The scripted predator chases the nearest visible prey, and swims in a straight line until it meets the wall when none is in view.

criteria: Given two prey in view at 0.2 and 0.4, when it acts, then it heads toward the one at 0.2.

nodes.title: A baseline agent sees only what the trained agent in the same world sees.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when the scripted fish observes, then a ball beyond 0.5 is hidden from it as in TANK-07.

nodes.title: Each agent is evaluated on 100 episodes, every agent in a world on the same 100 seeds.

criteria: Given a trained agent and both baselines in a world, when evaluated, then each has 100 scores from the same 100 starting seeds.

nodes.title: The learning curve is drawn with the dataviz skill: score against training progress, with the random and scripted agents' mean scores as reference lines.

criteria: Given a finished training run and its baselines' evaluations, when the chart is drawn, then it shows the curve and both reference lines on one axis.

nodes.title: "Beats a baseline" is tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill on the 100 evaluation scores of each; it passes only if the trained agent's mean is higher, significant at 5% after correction for the number of comparisons made in that world.

criteria: Given the trained and random agents' 100 scores each, when tested, then the result states the test, the corrected p-value and pass or fail.

nodes.title: The trained snake beats both the random and the scripted snake under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the Snake evaluations, when tested, then both comparisons pass.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish beats the random fish under EVAL-03.

criteria: Given the single-fish evaluations, when tested, then the comparison with the random fish passes; the same for the several-fish version.

nodes.title: In each fish version, the trained fish at least matches the scripted fish: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if the trained fish's mean survival is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 95% of the scripted fish's.

criteria: Given the trained fish's mean is 480 steps and the scripted fish's 490, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "trained mean ≤ 0.95 × 490".

nodes.title: In predator and prey, each trained side is compared under EVAL-03 with the random and scripted versions of that side, all playing against the scripted opponent.

criteria: Given a trained predator, when evaluated against the scripted prey, then its catches are tested against the random and scripted predators' catches against the same scripted prey.

nodes.title: The replay plays any saved agent on a chosen seed as a 2D animation of the world.

criteria: Given a saved trained snake and seed 42, when the replay is started, then the episode plays from its first step to its last.

nodes.title: The replay shows the step number and the current score.

criteria: Given a replay at step 150, when it is on screen, then "step 150" and the score so far are visible.

nodes.title: The replay can be paused, stepped one frame at a time, and run at speeds from 0.5× to 4×.

criteria: Given a paused replay, when "step" is pressed, then exactly one world step advances.

nodes.title: For agents that see only what is nearby, the replay draws each agent's sight circle.

criteria: Given the several-fish version, when replayed, then each fish has a 0.5-radius circle drawn around it.

nodes.title: A recorded episode can be watched again later exactly as it happened, without the agent or retraining.

criteria: Given a recorded episode, when reopened in a new session, then every frame matches the original.

nodes.title: Each world has one note of 1,000 words or fewer explaining why its learning method works.

criteria: Given a finished world, when its note is opened, then it explains the method's idea in ≤ 1,000 words.

nodes.title: The note includes the learning curve chart and the evaluation results.

criteria: Given the Snake note, when read, then it shows the EVAL-02 chart and the EVAL-04 results.

nodes.title: The note describes at least one behaviour seen in a replay, including a wrong or surprising one if seen.

criteria: Given the fish note, when read, then it names a behaviour and the seed of the replay where it shows.

nodes.title: The note states the reference check result and explains any gap.

criteria: Given the reference check result, when the note is read, then it states both scores and a reason for any difference.

nodes.title: The reference implementation is trained on the same world, with the same observations, actions, rewards and time limit as the hand-written learner.

criteria: Given the Snake check, when the reference trains, then it plays SNAKE-01..07's rules and stops within QR-01's limit.

nodes.title: The reference is evaluated on the same 100 seeds as EVAL-01.

criteria: Given the reference agent, when evaluated, then its 100 scores use the seeds of the hand-written agent's evaluation.

nodes.title: The hand-written learner lands in the reference's range: tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill, it passes only if its mean score is shown, at 5%, to be no worse than 80% of the reference's.

criteria: Given hand-written mean 18 and reference mean 20, when tested, then it passes if the test rejects "hand-written mean ≤ 0.8 × 20".

nodes.title: In the simultaneous regime, both sides learn at once, each always facing the other's current version.

criteria: Given a simultaneous run, when the predator updates, then the prey it trained against were the prey's latest version at that moment.

nodes.title: In the past-versions regime, a snapshot of each side is saved at least every 10% of the run, and each side trains against opponents drawn from all the other side's snapshots so far.

criteria: Given a past-versions run at 50% progress, when the predator plays a training episode, then its prey come from one of the prey's 5 or more saved snapshots.

nodes.title: Both regimes are compared side by side: every regime's final predator plays every regime's final prey for 100 evaluation episodes.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when compared, then a 2 × 2 table of predator and prey scores is produced.

nodes.title: Both regimes' learning curves are drawn on one chart with the dataviz skill, predator and prey shown separately.

criteria: Given both finished regimes, when the chart is drawn, then it shows four curves: each regime's predator and prey.

nodes.title: Each final agent plays the opponent's saved snapshots in order, showing whether later versions do better against it than earlier ones.

criteria: Given the final predator from either regime, when played against each prey snapshot for 100 episodes, then its catch rate per snapshot is reported in order.

nodes.title: Differences between the regimes are tested with the null-hypothesis-testing skill at 5%, corrected for the number of comparisons.

criteria: Given the 2 × 2 table's scores, when tested, then each regime difference is reported with its corrected p-value.

nodes.title: Snake and the fish tank are each signed off only when their evaluation passes, a replay of the trained agent is recorded, the learning curve chart exists, the note is complete and the reference check passes.

criteria: Given the trained predator fails EVAL-07 and the note explains why, when sign-off is checked, then predator and prey is finished.

criteria: Given the single fish beats random but falls short of the scripted fish, when the several-fish version is proposed, then it waits.

nodes.title: Evaluation seeds are never used in training.

criteria: Given any training run and the 100 evaluation seeds of its world, when the seeds it trained on are listed, then none is an evaluation seed.

nodes.title: Every training run's record holds what's needed to rerun it: its seed, its settings and the time it took.

criteria: Given a saved training record, when it is opened, then the seed, every setting and the wall-clock duration are present.
